query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix, whose overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures remain unclear, what single intervention could improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions, defines the operating limits of the prediction, cites supporting evidence from the introduction, and proposes a falsification experiment capable of resolving microscopic deformation during wear.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix can be improved by introducing a Ti content to the alloy, which will enhance the hot hardness and reduce the sliding wear rate under various temperatures and friction velocities.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Introduction of Ti content to the alloy
generation.conditions: Sliding wear conditions with varying temperatures and friction velocities
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a solid solution phase with enhanced hot hardness
generation.mechanism: The introduction of Ti content suppresses the formation of intermetallic compounds and enhances the hot hardness of the alloy, leading to improved wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved wear resistance compared to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating under identical conditions
generation.baseline: Wear resistance of the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating
generation.boundary: Temperature range: -200°C to 900°C, friction velocity range: 0.1 m/s to 10 m/s, wear depth range: 0.1 mm to 10 mm
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal Ti content and the underlying mechanisms of wear resistance improvement are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test with a pin-on-disc setup
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate of the Ti-containing alloy is not significantly lower than that of the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating under identical conditions, the hypothesis is falsified
